question: What price should a shopkeeper mark on a product costing him for Rs. 200 to gain 35% after allowing a discount of 25%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the ratio formula: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

200 ÷ MP = (100 − 25) ÷ (100 + 35)

200 ÷ MP = 75 ÷ 135 = 5 ÷ 9

MP = (200 × 9) ÷ 5 = 360

**∴ The correct answer is ₹360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Cost Price (CP) = ₹200, Profit% = 35%, Discount% = 25%

**Formula Used:** Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + P%)/100; Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 / (100 − D%)

 CP = ₹200 
 +35% Profit SP = ₹270 
 25% Disc. MP = ₹360 
 
 

⇒ Profit = 35% of ₹200 = (35 ÷ 100) × 200 = ₹70

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 200 + 70 = ₹270

⇒ Since a discount of 25% is given on MP, SP = 75% of MP

⇒ 75% of MP = ₹270

⇒ MP = 270 × (100 ÷ 75)

⇒ MP = 270 × (4 ÷ 3) = 90 × 4 = ₹360

**∴ The correct answer is ₹360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The relationship is given by the formula: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Gain%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100. It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price.
